newsitem.title: USA: Spaniard charged with shipping groceries to Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Spaniard charged with shipping groceries to Cuba.

text.p: A Spanish businessman remained in a U.S. detention centre on Monday awaiting trial for allegedly shipping food to Cuba in violation of the U.S. economic embargo against the communist-run state, officials said.
Javier Ferreiro, 45, was arrested last Tuesday at a shopping mall on Key Biscayne, a ritzy island offshore from Miami, on a charge of violating the Trading With The Enemy Act.
"We are accusing him of having shipping numerous containers of foodstuffs to Cuba between 1993 and 1996," U.S. Customs spokesman Michael Sheehan said.
A U.S. District Court judge on Thursday ordered Ferreiro held in pre-trial detention after prosecutors said he was a risk to flee.

Ferreiro, a Spanish national who lives in Havana, shipped canned vegetables, ketchup, sanitary napkins, disposable diapers and other goods to Cuba through the Dominican Republic, U.S. authorities said. He faced a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison and a $500,000 fine.
"It is illegal to ship goods from the United States to Cuba for any type of commercial venture, mattering not if you are an American citizen or not," Sheehan said.
The United States imposed its economic embargo on Fidel Castro's communist regime more than three decades ago.
